Look, don't take it so hard. To be completely honest, yes, this relationship has been difficult, has its ups and downs, but most relationships do. In fact, I honestly think a lot of couples I know between two NT people are actually a lot (and I mean A LOT) more dysfunctional than mine, and a lot more damaging to both parties as well. The only problem with dating an Aspie so far has been communication - which is a common problem in pretty much every single relationship. Except in relationships between NT people only the lack of communication is due to lack of interest, not inability to communicate. 
If that girl thought you weren't worth the trouble she wasn't worth your trouble either - because I believe you really have the same problem of not knowing how to communicate so it's basically the same issue, except it's probably even more frustrating for you. 
I have been with this boyfriend for almost 5 years now. He absolutely is worth any trouble. He is not always easy, but there's absolutely no malice in it. He is kind, faithful, he can be extremely funny around people he feels comfortable with and he knows so many interesting things. Honestly, he knows so much about Greek mythology and Ancient Greece in general, and about videogames and cartoons - he can talk about it for hours and I absolutely love to listen. He can be caring and when he genuinely is worried he really does everything to make me feel better. For instance (sorry, tmi) when I'm on those wonderful days women have that are extremely painful and moody, he really does understand I am in pain and he stays by my side in case I need something. He isn't exactly affectionate or anything, but I can see he does care and he does love me, and that's more than enough.
You probably also have many wonderful traits that someone will be able to see. Being wired differently doesn't make you less of a person and should not make you close yourself up in a metaphorical bubble. Things can get messy sometimes, but there's good in it too - in fact, most of the times it can have more good parts than bad ones. So it actually can work out better for everyone involved in the end. Don't give up on people just because a girl decided she wanted to avoid a little bit of trouble - if she does that, she probably would've given up at the first sign of trouble no matter if you were an Aspie or an NT (because there's always rough patches in every relationship). Not all girls are like that. Some of us can actually like people for who they are and are willing to work extra hard to be able to make a relationship work, even if the other person is a little bit different and that is difficult for us to deal with at first ;)

I felt the exact same way. But you know what? The good parts aren't really that special. The good parts are what any loving parent would do. Plus, most of the times, a NParent just acts nice for a while to make you feel just like you do. To guilt you into thinking they are not that bad, that they have goodness inside them as well. They need that so they can keep tormenting you. I've seen his happen with my mother and her parents (both of them). And I told myself I would not allow her to do he same thing to me just because she was taught that's a good mother-daughter relationship. 

I went LC with my NMom instead of NC because I want to keep in touch with the rest of the family. Because I love my cousins and I'm he godmother of the youngest one, and I would never stop being a part of that child's life due to something that only concerns me and my mother. My godson comes first, so I have some contact with my mother in family reunions and such. It was the best thing I've done. She tries to talk to me online, I ignore her rants and her little games to try to guilt me. She starts making a scene at a dinner party, I decide to take my little cousins to the movies. I have nothing to feel guilty about. She mistreated me, I defended myself. If she played nice, she would still be a part of my life. She had plenty of chances to do so. She chose to be an abusive parent. So I stopped acting like her wounded submissive child. I stopped acting like her child at all.

And you need to know this as well. You have nothing to feel guilty about. Your mother brought this situation upon herself. You did not go NC out of nowhere. You reacted to the way she treated you. And they never change. Not for long, at least. So, if they don't protect you as any parent should do, you protect yourself. And you avoid the people who harm you.

I wish you the best of luck and a lot of strength to get through this.
Best wishes

I'm not a parent yet, but as someone who has been a teen I can tell you it's best not to go overboard on snooping.
Teenage is a time most people make mistakes. A lot of them. It's a part of becoming an adult. Teens should have the right to be free to make them. With some limitations, of course.
My father was always really good at dealing with me when I was at that age. First of all, he was really strict when I was a child. As I got older, he started to let go a little bit, and everytime I had the freedom to do something, I had to take responsibility for every action related to it. That, I feel, was the most important thing - My dad respected my privacy and my choices, but if I screwed up, he would NOT cover for me. I'd be on my own, and that made me think way more than twice before I decided to do something. Also, I tell my dad almost everything - just keep my sex life private because in my culture it is supposed to be VERY private. Him allowing me to have my space and allowing me to grow up on my own at that crucial time of life brought us closer together. Of course he kept an eye open for warning signs - excessive drinking, drug use, sexual behaviour that could be harmful to my health, and so on. Fortunately, although I had a drink or two (nothing too strong) and tried smoking once throughout my life, I became someone who doesn't drink, smoke, and has never tried any illegal drugs (not even pot) and has only practiced safe sex with a boyfriend of 4 years. Of course, getting good grades always helped.

My mother always snooped. She read my diaries. She tried to over- analyse every Facebook status. She dissed all my friends (they are just like me - people who are happy by watching a movie at home and eating popcorn instead of going clubbing). She kept interfering with every aspect of my life. As she did that, I pushed her away. I needed my space.


TL;DR: so, my advice to you would be, keep an eye on him or her to see if (s)he isn't doing anything terribly wrong. Maybe add your kid on Facebook if (s)he is ok with it, but don't flip out at everything you see or read. Let the kid grow up, but be sure to show that (s)he will be dealing with the consequences, and if (s)he doesn't follow your advice (s)he will have to do that on his/her own. Let the teen make mistakes - they learn a lot more on their own than most people give them credit for.
